question: imd/acc listing review. imd/acc pays traders cashback as staked IMD through the Stacker 0x0457276d7b036818b3eddc1a4a3fceda61e9314d on chain 11155111. The project is the contract 0x2d5a03d5bab98a4a435edad11813373963bca8cc on chain 11155111, in the imd/acc ProjectRegistry 0x3a3bfcb65614292b0ec7c62f9e3a5dac003b920e. Should it be listed, so the cashback it pays earns points? Answer true only if every rule in the definitions holds for it, judged from its verified source code and on-chain state; otherwise answer false. definitions.trading: 0x2d5a03d5bab98a4a435edad11813373963bca8cc is a trading venue (for example a Uniswap v4 hook, a pool or a launchpad). Every call it can make to credit(trader, amount) on the Stacker happens while executing a trade, for the trader of that trade, with IMD from the fees of that trade. A wallet, an unverified contract, or a contract that can call credit outside a trade, for wallets it picks, or with IMD that is not from the trade fails this rule.
definitions.trader: The project never chooses who is credited. The trader may be the address the swap caller passes in hookData, as routers do, with the swap sender as the fallback; that address counts as the trader of that trade.
definitions.otherPayouts: Cashback that is not credited through the Stacker is allowed and simply earns no points: for example plain IMD paid when credit reverts, or a payout in another form when crediting is not possible. Such payouts never break the trading or rate rules.
definitions.rate: Each credit is 50 basis points of its trade (100 basis points = 1%), and that rate is between 25 and 100. If the rate can change, the code must keep it between 25 and 100 and 50 must be the rate in force now.
definitions.feeGuard: Split the trading fee into three parts: the cashback; the parts that come back to the owner or team (owner share, treasury, liquidity or reserves the owner or team can withdraw); and the parts that leave for good (burned tokens, prizes paid to others, fees to third parties, locked value as in lockedValue). The parts that leave for good must add up to at least the cashback. If the rate or the fee split can change, the code must keep this true for every allowed setting.
definitions.lockedValue: Liquidity or reserves that no owner or team wallet can ever withdraw count as leaving for good, even if the contract itself can move them between its own positions or pools.
definitions.beneficiary: 0x4b91078b2374c956a65f7af0999cae0a935e6821 must be the owner of 0x2d5a03d5bab98a4a435edad11813373963bca8cc, or a wallet its verified source or its official website names as its team or treasury.
definitions.evidence: Use the verified source published for this address on the chain named in the question, on its block explorer (Etherscan or Blockscout) or on Sourcify; a full or partial match on any one of them is verified source. Use on-chain reads at the latest block. Code with no verified source on any of them, or unreadable code, means false.
